newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan MPs want Scotland Yard in student murder.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan MPs want Scotland Yard in student murder.

text.p: Kenyan opposition parliament members on Friday urged the government to bring in British police to investigate the alleged murder of a student leader.
The parliament members were among hundreds of mourners at a funeral service for 23-year-old University of Nairobi student Solomon Muruli who was burnt in a blaze in his room on campus on February 23.

"The issue here is one of credibility. Few Kenyans have faith that the police and government can conduct a sincere investigation. We urge the government to bring in people who can do the job, we have in mind Scotland Yard," said Paul Muite, an MP.
Scotland Yard is historically the most famous department of the British police and its detectives have investigated past murders with political connotations in Kenya, a former British colony.
"The Yard's findings should also be made public," added Muite, a lawyer and representative from a constituency that includes Kikuyu campus, where Muruli was based and died.
Friday's church service, at the main Anglican All Saints Cathedral, was emotionally charged but went on peacefully. Dozens of riot police kept vigil outside the church.
Student speakers said security at campuses was rapidly declining and asked the government for urgent protection.

Education Minister Joseph Kamotho, secretary-general of the ruling KANU party, told Reuters he supported a pledge by the attorney-general that the government would leave no stone unturned until the truth was established.

"I think the security agencies should do their thorough, thorough investigation. I would like these independent security agencies to avail the truth because they should not blame the government," Kamotho said, referring to an investigation launched by the Kenyan police into the suspected murder.

Muruli's charred body was found early on Sunday in his room at a Nairobi University hostel at Kikuyu, 30 km (18 miles) outside the capital. Witnesses and a security officer said they heard an explosion shortly before.
On Monday Kenyan authorities closed down Nairobi and Egerton universities because of violent protests at Muruli's death.
Police spokesman Superintendent Peter Kimanthi said on Tuesday there was no evidence Muruli was killed by an explosion in his room because the body was "charred but not mutilated".
Kimanthi said police were investigating allegations Muruli received death threats in the week before his death and his reported abduction and torture for a week in November 1996.
